title: Golden-Ratio Spiral Benchmark — Estimation, Residuals and Model Selection
status: archive-generated quantitative geometry benchmark built from the recovered project spiral; established logarithmic-spiral mathematics, not a universal physical law
purpose: Turn the recovered equation r=a exp(b theta), with b_phi=2 ln(phi)/pi, into a reproducible hypothesis test rather than a visual motif. The benchmark estimates spiral center/orientation, fits the golden constraint against freer alternatives and requires held-out residual/model comparison before a target is described as following the project spiral.
why_promising: This is one of the strongest project equations because the mathematical object is exact and restrictive. A good model is allowed to lose: the golden hypothesis fixes its growth constant, so data can distinguish it from a generic logarithmic spiral, Archimedean spiral, power-law radial curve or flexible spline.

core_hypothesis.pitch: The constant angle between the tangent and local radial direction is arctan(1/b_phi); equivalently the tangent-to-circle pitch angle is arctan(b_phi) approximately 17.03 degrees.
core_hypothesis.curvature: kappa(theta)=1/[r(theta) sqrt(1+b_phi^2)] for a logarithmic spiral, so curvature falls by 1/phi per quarter turn as radius grows by phi.

observation_model.data: 2D coordinates p_i=(x_i,y_i) sampled from a candidate curve; 3D data require a separate projection/surface model rather than forced 2D fitting.
observation_model.warning: Center choice can strongly bias the fitted growth constant. Center/orientation must be estimated by a declared optimization procedure rather than selected by eye.

linearized_fit.golden_spiral: H_phi: y_i=alpha+b_phi x_i+epsilon_i with b_phi fixed
linearized_fit.noise: Start with epsilon_i~Normal(0,sigma^2) only as a baseline; inspect heteroscedasticity/autocorrelation and use a more appropriate error model if the measurement process requires it.

quarter_turn_residual_test.golden_prediction: Q=1 in the exact noiseless model
quarter_turn_residual_test.use: This supplies a local test that can reveal systematic departures even when a global spiral fit looks visually convincing.

competing_models.form: golden logarithmic spiral with b fixed to b_phi
generic logarithmic spiral r=a exp(b theta)
regularized flexible curve baseline; flexibility penalty must be included

model_selection.in_sample: Report residual structure and uncertainty, not only R^2.
model_selection.information_criteria: For comparable Gaussian-error fits, use AIC/BIC with the correct number of estimated parameters as one diagnostic.
model_selection.held_out: Prefer fitting one arc/range and evaluating predictive error on another arc/range when enough data exist.
model_selection.golden_success: H_phi performs comparably to or better than H_log despite one fewer free growth parameter and materially better than non-logarithmic baselines on held-out data.
model_selection.golden_rejection: A fitted b confidence/credible interval excludes b_phi, systematic quarter-turn residuals persist, or another model materially outperforms H_phi after complexity is accounted for.

dynamics_boundary.rule: Geometry does not imply a vortex, force, time evolution or energy law.
dynamics_boundary.upgrade_requirement: To claim spiral dynamics, add time-indexed data and a dynamical law for radial/angular velocity, then test whether the observed trajectory follows that law rather than merely tracing a similar static curve.

cross_scale_rule.requirement: A universal golden-spiral claim across plants, galaxies, bodies or project diagrams needs a dimensionless statistic tested independently in each domain with domain-appropriate nulls.
cross_scale_rule.anti_pattern: Do not select only visually spiral examples and then count successful fits; define the sampling population and negative cases first.

what_this_model_can_explain_if_successfu: Whether a chosen project or natural geometry is unusually consistent with the exact quarter-turn golden growth law rather than merely spiral-shaped.
Whether the recovered project spiral is a useful low-parameter compression of a real coordinate dataset.
Where and how an observed trajectory departs from exact self-similarity through residual structure.
failure_conditions: The fit depends strongly on manually chosen center/orientation.
A generic logarithmic spiral with free b substantially outperforms the golden constraint.
Archimedean/power/spline alternatives predict held-out points better.
Only a hand-picked subset of the curve supports the golden value.
A geometry fit is used as evidence for a physical mechanism without an independently specified dynamics.

external_references.source: Mediterranean Journal of Mathematics 2024 golden-spiral construction
external_references.use: Confirms the standard b=2 ln(phi)/pi golden logarithmic-spiral parameterization and quarter-turn phi scaling.

external_references.source: Statistical analysis of dynamic curves and sections
external_references.use: Example of quantitative logarithmic-spiral fitting to digitized natural curves rather than visual matching.
Useful caution that familiar natural objects are often logarithmic without being exactly golden; motivates model comparison rather than folklore.
